data.name: Alessandro
data.gender_notes: Alessandro is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Alessandro is derived from the Latin name Alexander, which means 'defender of the people'. In Christian tradition, Alessandro is associated with Saint Alexander of Rome, a brave and pious Roman soldier who was martyred during the persecution of Christians by Emperor Diocletian. The name Alessandro carries the meaning “Defender of mankind” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Alessandro usually hope their child will grow to embody defender of mankind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes bravery and devotion in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Alessandro belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Defender of mankind.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Alessandro total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Alessandro holds a rich cultural heritage as a popular male name across Europe, especially in Italian-speaking countries. Its association with notable historical figures like Alexander the Great, Emperor Alexander Severus, and Saint Alexander of Rome, has contributed to its esteemed status.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, Alessandro carries a spiritual significance as a reminder of the courage and faith displayed by Saint Alexander of Rome. Devout parents often choose this name for their child in hopes of instilling an unwavering commitment to faith and the protection of fellow believers, emulating the martyred saint's valiant spirit.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Alessandro, meaning "defender of mankind" in Italian, symbolizes the divine protection and strength granted to individuals in their personal journeys, reflecting God's love and care.

historical_references.reference: Born in Florence, Italy, in 1515, Alessandro de' Medici became the first duke of the House of Medici in 1537.
Historical records show that Alessandro Volta, an Italian physicist, invented the electric battery in 1800. The name Alessandro carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Alessandro remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.
